records.locator: Chapter XIII vv2–4, PDF273, original Sanskrit + Bhasin translation
records.source_paraphrase: The book lists Deepta, Svastha, Mudita, Shanta, Heena, Dukhita, Vikala, Khala, Kopi as nine planetary states, unlike the nine named Saravali Ch5.
records.critical_limit: Do not map homonymous Vikala/Khala directly to Saravali; definitions differ.

records.source_paraphrase: Heena is debilitation, Dukhita enemy sign, Vikala association with malefics, Khala defeated in war, Kopi with Sun in this text.
records.critical_limit: Compare Saravali's debility=Bhita, war defeat=Nipidita, combustion=Vikala, mark distinction as rule-system rather than mere lexical variant.

records.source_paraphrase: The nine avastha categories are explicitly connected to differentiated results during the governing planetary period, not just static natal personality.
records.critical_limit: Many outcomes are broad, moralized or medically unsuitable; effects of different states are not independent person-level successes.

records.locator: Chapter XIII Sun main period vv1–4, PDF275
records.source_paraphrase: Sun's highest exaltation degree versus general exaltation or adjacent signs is said to produce different graded period effects.
records.critical_limit: Source conditional hierarchy needs exact coordinate and period boundary before prospective test.

records.locator: Chapter XIV Mars period vv47–49, PDF300
records.source_paraphrase: Mars in exaltation sign but debilitated Navamsa is said to yield adverse outcomes, whereas Mars in debilitation sign and exalted Navamsa is said to yield good outcomes.
records.critical_limit: Specific D1/D9 contradiction counters simple sign-based direction; do not make health/family safety forecasts.

records.locator: Chapter XIV Mercury main period v10, PDF302
records.source_paraphrase: Mercury in a friendly sign during its ruling period is linked to fame through writings, distinct from general learning.
records.critical_limit: A dated publication/fame metric and explicit definition of friendly signs required; not retrospectively matched.

records.locator: Chapter XIV Mercury main period v30, PDF305
records.source_paraphrase: Mercury in the tenth during its period is associated with composing prose/poetry, religious initiation or public service.
records.critical_limit: Poetry and initiation are different target outcomes; historical ritual practices cannot prove liberation.

records.locator: Chapter XIV Mercury main period v31, PDF305
records.source_paraphrase: Mercury in eleventh during its period is said to produce gains through agriculture, trade, intellectual pursuits or charity.
records.critical_limit: Multiple alternative income channels may be base-rate broad; predeclare exact categories and misses.

records.locator: Chapter XIV Mercury main period v34, PDF305
records.source_paraphrase: Mercury's ruling period allegedly begins with material gain, gives honors in middle, and relationship conflict toward its final portion.
records.critical_limit: Fixed stage boundaries needed before score; multiple events within a period are dependent, not three independent validations.

records.locator: Chapter XVII v1, PDF370, Sanskrit/English printed image inspected
records.source_paraphrase: An extended duration Nakshatra and extended Tithi are said to produce health, wealth and auspicious outcomes.
records.critical_limit: Printed page clearly says CHAPTER—17; OCR reading CHAPTER-11 is false. Computation uses lunar calendar astronomical timings, not just zodiac signs.

records.locator: Chapter XVII v2 Translator's Note, PDF370
records.source_paraphrase: Bhasin adds Kshaya Tithi interpretation and relative one, ten, and lakh effect magnitudes for Tithi, Nakshatra and Lagna.
records.critical_limit: Clearly labeled TRANSLATOR'S NOTE, not separately quoted ancient verse. Do not promote as original Venkatesha.

records.source_paraphrase: Adverse outcomes assigned to malefics in angular houses are qualified by a named alternative school attributed to Acharya Shankar requiring malefic ascendant-lord involvement.
records.critical_limit: High-stakes negative body/lifetime references historical only; preserve both without picking after outcomes.

records.source_paraphrase: Royal yoga allegedly weakened by planets' debilitation Navamsas can still persist if angular/trinal benefics or an own-navamsa significator with Jupiter's aspect occurs.
records.critical_limit: Moral/medical narrative not valid personal forecast; no permissive posthoc rescue when rule is unfulfilled.

records.source_paraphrase: Sun, Mars and Saturn defined dry, Moon/Venus watery, Mercury/Jupiter conditionally watery depending on signs, with a nonstandard set of watery signs.
records.critical_limit: Different from modern elemental systems; code school-specific sign classification if ever tested.

records.source_paraphrase: Badhaka/obstructive houses assigned eleventh for movable ascendants, ninth for fixed and seventh for dual, with lords/occupants; other obstruction indicators added.
records.critical_limit: Source itself has complex multi-signal precedence; do not score individual difficulties without fully frozen feature pipeline.

records.locator: Chapter VI vv33–35, PDF168, original Sanskrit and English
records.source_paraphrase: Complex seventh lord and divisional configurations allegedly predict a person with 100, 200 or 300 wives.
records.critical_limit: Historically extraordinary/implausible multi-wife category; no safe person-level predictions. Source premise requires astronomical physical feasibility check.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath's translation assigns Mars fixed signification of younger relatives, brother-in-law and mother, with a specific Sanskrit kinship expression.
records.critical_limit: Kinship/sex and fixed vs natural karaka distinctions preserved; applications beyond literal Sanskrit must be labeled commentary.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath proposes changing a transmitted kinship word to 'sister's son' on a belief that Parashara would not repeat or make an error.
records.critical_limit: Conjectural correction; no independently collated manuscript evidence, no right to overwrite existing source wording.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath suggests a received word sukra (Venus) should instead be sakra (Indra) in a Jupiter fixed-significator verse.
records.critical_limit: Presented as possible textual corruption; his spiritual rationale does not prove Sanskrit manuscript variant.

records.source_paraphrase: Jaimini sutras assign Mercury to maternal kin/uncles and Jupiter to paternal grandfather, husband, children and deity in Rath's rendering.
records.critical_limit: Compare BPHS quoted separately; source-specific cultural lineage assumptions.

records.source_paraphrase: Jaimini sutras associate Venus with in-law/maternal family and Saturn with elder siblings/relatives.
records.critical_limit: Modern gender assumptions culturally context-bound; absence of spouse facts not failure of natal personality.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath's lesson defines 'stronger' for competing fixed parent-significator planets as the more afflicted/punishing for a mortality analysis.
records.critical_limit: Not a direct Jaimini sutra statement, not evidence of accurate familial mortality prediction or safe individual risk assessment.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath retrospectively selects several already-public family deaths and illnesses to illustrate Sthira Karaka period rules.
records.critical_limit: No independently frozen forecast or adversarial control. Never count as measured prediction success.

records.locator: Lesson16 BPHS 34.34 quote and discussion, PDF353–354
records.source_paraphrase: Rath quotes a BPHS twelve-house primary natural significator list, then interprets every house lord as carrying those planet traits when placed in other houses.
records.critical_limit: House-lord personality transfer is Rath's explanatory extrapolation, not verbatim BPHS verse; avoid double counting across Jaimini/Parashara.

independence_policy: Each literary rule and editor illustration is not a distinct genuine human test. Narratives of known public figures remain DEVELOPMENT_ONLY. Original Sanskrit, published translation, editorial emendation and modern spiritual/health inferences are separate layers.
